process_area.title: Standalone Selling Price, Allocation & Deferred-Revenue Measurement

fields.Participants: Pricing (VS-01.2), Merchandising (VS-01), Services (VS-12/VS-66), Analytics (VS-28), Controller, External Auditor
fields.Trigger: New multi-element arrangement; annual SSP refresh; market-price shift
fields.Volume: SSP for ~ installation service, design service, warranty, loyalty points, subscription, bundle components, retail-media placement

workflows.name: Standalone Selling Price (SSP) Methodology & Estimation Framework

Automation Opportunity: - SSP register auto-fed from observable separate-sales data; market/labor-cost shift alerts triggering review; allocation-engine consumption of SSP
Controls: - CTL-702 (ensure controlled execution — Standalone Selling Price, Allocation & Deferred-Revenue Measurement (PA-157.2).)
- CTL-702: documented SSP hierarchy; SSP register versioned and Controller-approved; judgment estimates auditor-reviewed
Cross-references: - links to VS-01.2/VS-158 (pricing/cost), VS-12/VS-66 (services), VS-106/VS-102 (cost inputs), W4634 (allocation), W4644 (audit)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Judgment-heavy SSP risk**: Obligations never sold separately (installation, design) require expected-cost-plus-margin estimates the auditor may challenge → prior-period adjustment; mitigated by documented methodology and early auditor engagement
- **Stale-SSP risk**: An SSP not refreshed after a labor/commodity shift mis-allocates revenue; mitigated by the refresh cadence and market-shift trigger
System Touchpoints: - SSP register (revenue module); pricing/cost masters (VS-01.2/VS-158); analytics (VS-28); audit evidence repository (VS-88)
Time Estimate: - ~5–10 days annual SSP refresh; ~1–2 days per new-obligation SSP determination

steps.activity: Define the SSP hierarchy/methodology per obligation type: (a) observable standalone price first (when the obligation is also sold separately — e.g., extended warranty, some installation); (b) market-adjusted assessment; (c) residual approach only when permitted; (d) expected-cost-plus-margin for obligations never sold separately (installation bundled only)

Maintain the SSP register with per-obligation SSP, data source, refresh date, and estimation variables (e.g., installation labor rate, warranty expected cost + margin); refresh on the cadence and on material market shifts (commodity/labor — links VS-106/VS-102)
Submit the SSP methodology and any judgment-heavy estimates to the External Auditor for review at year-end (and pre-launch of new arrangements); document conclusions and retain evidence

fields.Trigger: Each multi-element sale (bundle/kit, product+install, product+warranty+points); SSP refresh
fields.Volume: Every bundle/kit sale (VS-92); every product+installation sale (VS-12); points earned on every POS sale

Automation Opportunity: - Relative-SSP auto-allocation at POS/order; out-of-range exception report; allocation audit trail for every transaction
Controls: - CTL-702 (ensure controlled execution — Standalone Selling Price, Allocation & Deferred-Revenue Measurement (PA-157.2).)
- CTL-702: allocation engine Controller-approved; sample-tested quarterly; SSP within range; exceptions reviewed
Cross-references: - links to W4633 (SSP), VS-92 (kit), VS-12 (install), VS-13 (points), W544 (work order), W4648 (controls)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Mis-allocation risk**: A bug or stale SSP in the allocation engine mis-states revenue across obligations and periods at scale (every POS/bundle transaction); mitigated by sample validation and SSP freshness
- **Discount-allocation error risk**: A bundle discount not allocated to the obligations to which it relates distorts per-obligation revenue; mitigated by the relative-SSP rule and exception review
System Touchpoints: - Allocation engine (revenue module); kit/BOM (VS-92.1); service work order (W544); loyalty engine (VS-13); GL (VS-17.1)
Time Estimate: - ~2–3 days/quarter allocation validation + sample testing; per-setup ~2–4 days

steps.activity: Configure the allocation engine: distribute the transaction price across each performance obligation based on relative SSP (W4633); apply any allocation-specific discount to the obligations to which it relates

Validate allocation on sample transactions (bundle, product+install, product+warranty+points) — confirm the sum of allocations equals transaction price and each obligation's allocation is within SSP range; investigate out-of-range allocations
Post each allocation to the correct revenue/deferred-revenue GL by obligation and period; route exceptions (manual override, non-standard contract) to Revenue Accounting review

fields.Participants: Gift-card ops (VS-54), Analytics (VS-28), Controller, External Auditor
fields.Trigger: Monthly gift-card liability review (VS-54); annual breakage recalc
fields.Volume: Outstanding gift-card liability (VS-54 W28); ~ gift cards sold/redeemed monthly

workflows.name: Gift-Card Breakage Estimation, Recognition & Remote-Redemption Testing

Automation Opportunity: - Redemption-curve auto-computation; breakage candidate-list with remote-redemption flag; auto-reconcile liability GL to feed
Controls: - CTL-702 (ensure controlled execution — Standalone Selling Price, Allocation & Deferred-Revenue Measurement (PA-157.2).)
- CTL-702: breakage recognized only at remote-redemption (proportionate); methodology auditor-reviewed; liability GL reconciled monthly
Cross-references: - links to VS-54 (gift card), W28 (liability), W4636 (analogous loyalty breakage), W4641 (close), W4643 (disclosure)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Premature-breakage risk**: Recognizing breakage before redemption is remote overstates revenue (aggressive accounting) — a classic audit finding; mitigated by the remote-redemption test and proportionate recognition
- **Limited-history risk**: BuildRight's gift-card program is relatively new → breakage estimate rests on thin data; mitigated by conservative estimation and auditor review
System Touchpoints: - Gift-card module (VS-54 W28); GL contract-liability (VS-17.1); analytics (VS-28); month-end close (W9A)
Time Estimate: - ~2–3 days/month gift-card liability + breakage accounting; ~3–5 days annual recalc

steps.activity: Compute the historical redemption pattern (aging of unredeemed balances, redemption curve) from gift-card transaction history; estimate the breakage rate (portion expected never to be redeemed)

Recognize breakage revenue ONLY when the likelihood of redemption becomes remote (per PFRS 15 ¶B43) — proportionally based on the redemption pattern, not on a fixed time; document the remote-redemption determination

Reconcile the gift-card liability GL (W28) to the gift-card outstanding-balance feed; post breakage revenue journal during month-end close (W9A); re-assess the estimate with full-year data at year-end

fields.Participants: Loyalty (VS-13), Analytics (VS-28), Actuarial support, Controller, External Auditor
fields.Volume: Points earned on 2.8M monthly POS transactions (600K members); points liability GL

workflows.name: Loyalty-Points Liability Measurement, Fair-Value & Forfeiture Adjustment

Automation Opportunity: - Redemption-triggered auto-release; engine-to-GL auto-reconcile; drift-alert triggering re-estimation
Controls: - CTL-702 (ensure controlled execution — Standalone Selling Price, Allocation & Deferred-Revenue Measurement (PA-157.2).)
- CTL-702: documented fair-value/redemption methodology (auditor-reviewed); monthly engine-to-GL reconcile; quarterly true-up
Cross-references: - links to VS-13 (loyalty), W104/W17 (points), W4631 (obligation setup), W4635 (breakage analog), W4643 (disclosure)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Estimation-volatility risk**: Redemption-rate shifts swing the liability and period revenue; mitigated by quarterly true-up and documented methodology
- **Engine-to-GL drift risk**: (as W4631) mitigated by monthly reconcile
System Touchpoints: - Loyalty engine (VS-13 W17/W104); POS earning feed (VS-08); deferred-revenue GL (VS-17.1); analytics (VS-28)

steps.activity: Determine the per-point fair value (standalone selling price of points) and the redemption-rate/forfeiture estimate; refresh quarterly using actual redemption behavior and tier mix

Recognize deferred revenue to revenue as points are redeemed; for points expected to forfeit, recognize the breakage-style portion when redemption is remote (mirroring W4635); true-up cumulative catch-up each period
Reconcile the points-deferred-revenue GL to the loyalty-engine liability (W104/W17) monthly; investigate redemption-rate drift > threshold and re-estimate

fields.Volume: Subscription contracts (VS-47); extended-warranty contracts (VS-53); growing base

Automation Opportunity: - Per-contract amortization schedule auto-generated; auto-post during close; exception report for abnormal patterns
Controls: - CTL-702 (ensure controlled execution — Standalone Selling Price, Allocation & Deferred-Revenue Measurement (PA-157.2).)
- CTL-702: revenue deferred and amortized over the coverage period; schedule reconciled to GL monthly; cancellations routed to estimate-update
Cross-references: - links to VS-47 (subscription), VS-53 (warranty), W33 (warranty liability), W4638 (variable consideration), W4641 (close)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Period-mismatch risk**: Recognizing subscription/warranty revenue up-front (rather than over the period) overstates period revenue; mitigated by the deferred-amortization rule
- **Renewal/cancellation handling risk**: Mis-handling mid-period cancellations/renewals distorts the schedule; mitigated by estimate-update routing (W4638)
System Touchpoints: - Subscription module (VS-47); warranty module (VS-53 W33); deferred-revenue schedule (revenue module); GL (VS-17.1); month-end close (W9A)

steps.activity: For subscription services (VS-47) and extended warranties (VS-53), recognize revenue over the coverage/service period (straight-line unless usage-based is more faithful); defer the full consideration at sale

Run the monthly deferred-revenue amortization schedule (per contract, by period); post the amortization journal during close (W9A); handle renewals, cancellations, and refunds as estimate updates (W4638)
Reconcile the subscription/warranty deferred-revenue GL to the active-contract schedule; investigate contracts with no amortization or abnormal patterns

fields.Participants: Trade/Government ops (VS-11/VS-46), Rebate ops (VS-39), Tax (VS-79/VS-85), Controller
fields.Trigger: Variable consideration in a contract (rebates, refunds, volume discounts, SC/PWD mandatory discounts, price-freeze, trade-in top-up); quarterly estimate update
fields.Volume: Vendor rebates (VS-39), SC/PWD discounts (VS-85), price-freeze (DTI), refunds/returns (~2% return rate), trade-in variance (VS-155)

workflows.name: Variable Consideration, Constraint & Estimate-Update (Rebates, Refunds, SC/PWD, Price-Freeze)

Automation Opportunity: - Expected-value estimation from historical data; constraint-test checklist; cumulative catch-up auto-posting
Controls: - CTL-702 (ensure controlled execution — Standalone Selling Price, Allocation & Deferred-Revenue Measurement (PA-157.2).)
- CTL-702: constraint applied (no highly-probable reversal); estimates updated quarterly; judgment-heavy items Controller/CFO-reviewed
Cross-references: - links to VS-39 (rebate), VS-85 (SC/PWD), VS-32 (refunds), VS-155 (trade-in), W4641 (close), W4643 (disclosure)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Reversal risk**: Recognizing variable consideration too aggressively → significant revenue reversal when the uncertainty resolves (audit finding); mitigated by the constraint test
- **Estimate-staleness risk**: Out-of-date estimates mis-state period revenue; mitigated by quarterly update and cumulative catch-up
System Touchpoints: - Rebate module (VS-39); returns/refund liability (VS-32); SC/PWD discount (VS-85); trade-in (VS-155); revenue module variable-consideration ledger; GL (VS-17.1)
Time Estimate: - ~3–5 days/quarter variable-consideration update across contract types

steps.activity: Identify variable consideration in each contract type; estimate the amount using the expected-value or most-likely-amount method; apply the constraint (recognize only to the extent a significant revenue reversal is NOT highly probable when the uncertainty resolves)

Update estimates each reporting period; record cumulative catch-up adjustments in the period of estimate change; coordinate with the relevant operational flow (rebate accrual VS-39, SC/PWD VS-85, refund liability VS-32)
Document the constraint assessment for judgment-heavy variable consideration (e.g., large project volume rebates, trade-in buy-back variance VS-155); retain evidence for audit

fields.Trigger: Long-term project with deferred payment (VS-11/VS-46); large advance/prepayment (VS-15 W498); annual review
fields.Volume: Project/G2G deferred-payment contracts; vendor advance payments (W498); subscription prepayments

Automation Opportunity: - Financing-component screen on contracts with payment-delivery gap >12 months; discount-rate feed from Treasury policy
Controls: - CTL-702 (ensure controlled execution — Standalone Selling Price, Allocation & Deferred-Revenue Measurement (PA-157.2).)
- CTL-702: >12-month/materiality screen applied; discount rate Treasury-aligned and documented; practical expedients basis recorded
Cross-references: - links to VS-11.2/VS-46.2 (project/G2G), W498 (prepayment), VS-18 (treasury/discount), W4643 (disclosure)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Missed-financing-component risk**: Failing to discount a long deferred-payment contract mis-states revenue and omits interest — audit finding; mitigated by the >12-month/materiality screen
- **Discount-rate judgment risk**: Inappropriate discount rate distorts the adjustment; mitigated by Treasury alignment and documented rationale
System Touchpoints: - Project module (VS-11.2); AP prepayment (W498); Treasury discount-rate policy (VS-18); revenue module; GL (VS-17.1)
Time Estimate: - ~1–2 days/quarter assessment; per-contract ~2–4 hours when triggered

steps.activity: For contracts where payment timing differs significantly from delivery (e.g., project retainage over 12+ months, large customer deposits, long prepayment cycles), assess whether a significant financing component exists (>12 months and material)
Where a significant financing component exists, adjust the transaction price for the time value of money (discount); separate interest revenue/expense; document the discount-rate rationale

For the practical expedients (no financing component if ≤12 months, or if consideration is variable and the financing element is indeterminate), document the basis; align with Treasury's discount-rate policy (VS-18)

fields.Trigger: Incremental contract-acquisition cost (sales commission); cost-to-fulfill (setup); annual impairment review
fields.Volume: Sales commissions (VS-11/VS-107 trade & key-account); fulfillment setup costs (subscription/marketplace onboarding)

workflows.name: Contract Costs — Cost-to-Obtain & Cost-to-Fulfill (Capitalization, Amortization & Impairment)

Automation Opportunity: - Auto-amortization in proportion to revenue recognition; impairment trigger on contract-status change (lost/curtailed); commission-to-contract-cost linking
Controls: - CTL-702 (ensure controlled execution — Standalone Selling Price, Allocation & Deferred-Revenue Measurement (PA-157.2).)
- CTL-702: capitalization criteria applied; amortization aligned to revenue pattern; impairment reviewed quarterly; asset GL reconciled
Cross-references: - links to VS-11/VS-107 (sales), W228 (commissions), VS-102 (comp), VS-47/VS-95 (subscription/marketplace), W4643 (disclosure)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Over-capitalization risk**: Capitalizing costs that don't meet the incremental/enhancing test inflates the asset and defers expense; mitigated by the cost-classification criteria
- **Impairment miss risk**: Failing to impair a capitalized cost whose contract is lost/curtailed → overstated asset; mitigated by the periodic impairment review tied to contract status
System Touchpoints: - Commission module (W228); contract-cost asset GL (VS-17.1); amortization schedule; impairment review (revenue module)

steps.activity: Identify incremental costs to obtain a contract (e.g., sales commissions tied to winning a trade/key-account/G2G contract) and capitalize; expense other acquisition costs as incurred

Identify costs to fulfill that generate/enhance resources used to satisfy obligations (e.g., subscription/marketplace onboarding setup) and capitalize; amortize both cost categories in proportion to revenue recognition (or straight-line if more faithful); apply the ≤12-month practical expedient for commissions where eligible

Assess impairment of capitalized contract costs each period (expected economic benefits no longer expected); coordinate amortization with the sales-comp accrual (W228 trade commissions) and reconcile the asset GL
